claude.sample_unit: consent forms from academic medical centers

links.outcome: Reading level of existing surgical consent forms versus average American reading level
links.effect: Original consent forms had median Flesch-Kincaid Reading Level 13.9 and Reading Ease 35.3 (college level), versus 8th grade average American reading level.
links.quote: Prior to LLM processing, surgical consent forms had a median Flesch-Kincaid Reading Level of 13.9 (IQR = 12.8–14.2; Fig. 1B ) and Flesch Reading Ease score of 35.3 (IQR = 33.0–39.9; Fig. 1C ), both denoting a college education level of readability difficulty.

links.outcome: Readability of consent forms before vs after GPT-4 plain-language simplification
links.effect: Reading level fell from 13.9 to 8.9 (P = 0.004); Reading Ease rose from 35.3 to 63.8 (P < 0.001); passive voice fell from 38.4% to 20.0%; word rarity fell.
links.quote: After simplification, there was a significant decrease in the Reading Level (before = 13.9 vs. after = 8.9, P = 0.004) and improvement in Reading Ease (before = 35.3 vs. after = 63.8 P < 0.001) from the reading level of a college freshman to that of an 8th grade student.

links.outcome: Independent expert medical and legal review confirming content preserved after AI simplification
links.effect: Three physicians agreed content remained comparable for all 15 forms; malpractice attorney found all 15 pairs met same legal sufficiency; surgeon review of de novo forms found no significant inaccuracies.
links.quote: Additionally, one medical malpractice defense attorney (PG) reviewed the consents before and after simplification and determined that all 15 consent pairs met the same legal sufficiency.

unlisted_practices: Using GPT-4 to simplify surgical consent forms to average American reading level with expert medical and legal review
Using GPT-4 to generate de novo procedure-specific consent forms checked with a validated rubric and subspecialty surgeon review

openai.sample_unit: surgical consent forms (15 existing generic forms plus 5 GPT-4-generated procedure-specific forms)

links.effect: Median grade level decreased from 13.9 to 8.9 (P = 0.004).
links.quote: After simplification, there was a significant decrease in the Reading Level (before = 13.9 vs. after = 8.9, P = 0.004) and improvement in Reading Ease (before = 35.3 vs. after = 63.8 P < 0.001) from the reading level of a college freshman to that of an 8th grade student.

links.effect: Average word rarity decreased from 2845 to 1328 (P < 0.001).
links.quote: Moreover, the average rarity of the words used in the text decreased significantly after simplification (before = 2845 vs. after = 1328, P < 0.001; Fig. 1E ).

links.outcome: Expert review of generated consent forms
links.effect: For five forms, subspecialty surgeon review yielded no wording changes or significant clinical inaccuracies requiring correction.
links.quote: Despite the variety of procedures encapsulated by this task, procedure-specific expert review by subspecialty surgeons (WFA, AET, NRS, NRS, and TJL, respectively) yielded no wording changes or significant clinical inaccuracies requiring correction.

links.outcome: surgical consent form readability after AI simplification
links.effect: Readability improved from college freshman to 8th-grade level (P=0.004), matching the average American reading level, while procedure-specific forms averaged a 6th-grade reading level
links.quote: Readability improved from an average college freshman to an 8th-grade level (P = 0.004), matching the average American's reading level.

unlisted_practices: Using large language models to simplify surgical consent forms to match patient reading levels
Multidisciplinary medical, legal, and subspecialty surgeon review to validate AI-simplified and AI-generated consent forms
